newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's CPP rate falls in January vs December.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's CPP rate falls in January vs December.

text.p: Mexico's CPP fell 289 basis points in January from December to 24.08 percent, the Banco de Mexico said. The CPP, the average bank cost of borrowing for the public, was at 26.97 percent in December.
The central bank also said that the CCP, the average bank term deposit cost measured in pesos in Mexican banks, was 25.29 percent for the month.
The CCP will eventually become a substitute for the CPP, with the aim of better reflecting the cost of those term deposits for the banks.
The Banco de Mexico also said that the CCP-UDIs, the CPP measured in UDIs, an inflation-indexed investment unit, was at 6.61 percent for January, down from 7.27 percent in December.

Banco de Mexico has said it publishes the various rates in order to give a better idea to the public of the cost of borrowing, and so that banks can only use the reference rates signalled by the central bank, which it hopes will better reflect market conditions.
